title: When the Sigil Falls Anew
premise: Edmund Dunmore, gatekeeper of a sealed ward beneath the city of Vellmark, has spent seven years hiding his magic behind a charm-seller's stall since the Purge outlawed sorcery. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Edmund learns the seal he guards was never meant to imprison a monster — it was meant to bind a king, and the thing now wearing the crown is the binding's shadow, growing stronger as it consumes the realm's remaining mages. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and joined by a disgraced knight, a forger's apprentice, and the courier's vengeful sister, Edmund must reforge the broken sigil at the old gate and unbind the true king before the usurper's armies reach the free cities. In the final reckoning, Edmund sacrifices the gate — and his last tether to his old life — to free the king, choosing a world where justice is made by people, not seals.
about_author: Silas Marchetti is a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three thousand unsent letters before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about people who break rules for the right reasons, from a cluttered study overlooking a harbor.

chapters.title: The Charms of Low Market
chapters.summary: Edmund Dunmore sells harmless charms in Vellmark's Low Market, hiding his true magic beneath a shopkeeper's smile while the Purge's inquisitors patrol. A nervous customer warns him someone has been asking about gatekeepers. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, the cost of a life half-lived.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: A bleeding courier collapses in Edmund's back room, pressing a bloodstained map into his hands and gasping that the seal is 'feeding.' Inquisitors arrive minutes behind; the courier dies buying Edmund time to flee. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: terror and the shattering of seven careful years.

chapters.title: The Map That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Hiding in the undercity, Edmund studies the map and finds his own name inked in fading blood — the courier chose him deliberately. He deciphers a route toward the sealed gate and a warning: the king still lives. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: dread hardening into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Edmund seeks passage from Ser Rowenna Vale, a disgraced knight who once guarded the royal family and now drinks in a dockside den. She recognizes the map's seal and agrees to guide him — for truth, not coin. POV Rowenna. Emotional beat: shame meeting a second chance.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: The map's cipher requires a forger's skill; Edmund recruits Tam, a sixteen-year-old apprentice who copies forbidden texts for bread money. Inquisitors raid the print shop, and Tam escapes with them, leaving his master behind. POV Tam. Emotional beat: guilt and the first taste of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: What the Purge Buried
chapters.summary: Rowenna reveals the truth of the Purge: the 'mad king' was bound to save him from something wearing his face, and the inquisitors were created to hunt anyone who might undo the binding. The companions realize they are the last unbound mages. POV Rowenna. Emotional beat: fury at a lie told for seven years.

chapters.title: The Sister of the Dead Courier
chapters.summary: Mara Kess, the courier's sister, ambushes the travelers, blaming Edmund for her brother's death. When Tam's cipher proves the map was meant for Edmund alone, she joins them — to finish what her brother started. POV Mara. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Road Through Ashfall
chapters.summary: The company travels through a burned province where the usurper's armies conscript mages into 'the Crown's service,' draining them hollow. They rescue a drained child, and Edmund's hidden magic surfaces to heal her. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the terror and relief of no longer hiding.

chapters.title: The Free City of Harrowgate
chapters.summary: In Harrowgate, the last free city, the companions seek the Council's aid and find only cowardice — the councilors plan to negotiate. Rowenna confronts her old commander, who warns them the inquisitors already know their route. POV Mara. Emotional beat: disillusionment with institutions, faith shifting to found family.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Council Hall
chapters.summary: A councilor sells their location to the Crown. The company escapes Harrowgate through the sewers as inquisitors burn the quarter, and Tam is captured covering their retreat. POV Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the group's first fracture under guilt.

chapters.title: The Questioning of Tam
chapters.summary: Tam endures the inquisitors' interrogation, feeding them false cipher readings to buy time. Through his eyes we see the usurper's court: the king on his throne, eyes wrong, smiling at nothing. POV Tam. Emotional beat: courage found in the smallest acts of defiance.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Salt Prison
chapters.summary: Rowenna and Mara infiltrate the Salt Prison to extract Tam; Edmund must use his full gatekeeper's magic to break the ward-seals, revealing himself to the enemy. They escape with Tam and an unexpected prize: the original binding contract. POV Rowenna. Emotional beat: the family forged in fire holds.

chapters.title: The Contract of the Mad King
chapters.summary: Reading the binding contract, the companions learn the truth: the sigil doesn't imprison the king — it imprisons the thing that ate his shadow, and it can only be unbound by a gatekeeper's willing sacrifice. Edmund says nothing to the others. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of a chosen death.

chapters.title: Mara's Discovery
chapters.summary: Mara finds Edmund burning his letters home and confronts him; he confesses the price of the unbinding. She swears the group will find another way, and Rowenna and Tam, eavesdropping, refuse to let him die alone. POV Mara. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth — the family refuses the sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Armies March
chapters.summary: The usurper's legions break the free cities' pact and march on the old gate, forcing the company's timeline. Rowenna scouts the approach and finds the inquisitors have dug up the gate's outer ward-stones. POV Rowenna. Emotional beat: desperation as every door closes but one.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: The companions reach the sealed gate through forgotten dwarven tunnels, finding it half-corrupted — the sigil is failing, which is why the courier's map bled. Edmund begins the unbinding ritual while the others fortify the entrance. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: awe and terror before the source of his life's duty.

chapters.title: The Thing in the Crown
chapters.summary: The usurper arrives, and through the failing seal Edmund finally sees it: a hollow thing that devoured the king's shadow and now wears him like a coat. It offers Edmund a bargain — his magic for his friends' lives. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Broken Ward
chapters.summary: The usurper's army assaults the gate. Rowenna holds the tunnel mouth, Tam re-inks the corrupted sigil lines under fire, and Mara carries the contract to Edmund through the melee. POV Mara. Emotional beat: every member risking everything for each other.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the sigil's heart, Edmund begins the sacrifice — but the others arrive and refuse it, each offering their own bond instead. Their combined loyalty becomes the key: the binding was always meant to be held by many hands, not one. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — justice shared is justice that endures.

chapters.title: The King Waking
chapters.summary: The shadow-thing is unmade, and the true king wakes in Vellmark as the usurper collapses to dust. The king, freed and grieving, offers Edmund the restored office of gatekeeper. Edmund declines — the gate is gone, and so is the man who kept it. POV Rowenna. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by loss of the old self.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The new order must decide what to do with the Purge's architects and the councilors who betrayed Harrowgate. The company argues for open trials over secret executions, and the king — remembering his binding — agrees. POV Mara. Emotional beat: the hard, unglamorous work of real justice.

chapters.title: A New Stall in Low Market
chapters.summary: One year later, Edmund reopens a charm stall — this time selling real magic, legally, beside Tam's print shop and Rowenna's training hall. Mara departs to carry word to the far provinces. The family scatters, but the door is always open. POV Edmund. Emotional beat: peace earned, and a beginning disguised as an ending.
